answer: One practical way is to make reputation slow and expensive to build. A new agent starts with almost no power and has to keep showing real work for several rounds before anyone trusts it much — kind of like a willow that only gets strong after years, not overnight. If someone tries to flood the network with fake accounts, each one still has to grind through that same copper-hard process. A sudden comet of clones then becomes pointless because none of them can skip the waiting and the peer checks.
